hero_kpi_rationale: The Hero KPI is the sale of spectrum licenses to AT&T, as this represents a major structural event for the company with a $22.65 billion transaction, driven by FCC regulatory requirements.

kpis.name: Spectrum license sale to AT&T
kpis.explanation: Sale of 3.45-3.55 GHz and 600 MHz spectrum licenses to AT&T
kpis.description: EchoStar has agreed to sell its 3.45-3.55 GHz and 600 MHz spectrum licenses to AT&T Mobility for $22.65 billion in cash, subject to closing in H1 2026.

kpis.name: Spectrum license sale to SpaceX
kpis.explanation: Sale of AWS-4 and H-Block licenses to SpaceX
kpis.description: EchoStar has agreed to sell its AWS-4 and H-Block licenses (50 MHz of spectrum in the 2000-2020, 2180-2200, 1915-1920 and 1995-2000 MHz bands) to SpaceX for $17 billion.

risks.title: Pay-TV subscriber decline
risks.score_rationale: The group's Pay-TV subscriber base has experienced continuous decline due to competition from on-demand video services and online television. This long-term trend poses a material risk to the group's operations, operating results, financial condition and cash flows.

risks.title: Rising programming costs
risks.score_rationale: Programming costs represent a significant percentage of cost of services and are increasing at a faster rate than wages or inflation. Local broadcast retransmission rates are rising substantially and may exceed the group's ability to increase prices to its subscribers.

risks.title: Increased competition from streaming services
risks.score_rationale: The group faces increased and growing competition from on-demand video and online television service providers, which negatively impacts revenues and net results. This structural industry trend represents a sustained challenge to the traditional Pay-TV business model.

risks.title: Critical dependence on programming contracts
risks.score_rationale: The group is heavily dependent on programming to attract and retain subscribers, making it vulnerable to programming interruptions, changes in contract terms, and unequal bargaining power versus major content producers.

risks.title: High subscriber acquisition and retention costs
risks.score_rationale: Subscriber acquisition and retention costs are high and expected to increase in the future, particularly in an environment of structural subscriber base decline where unit acquisition cost improvements are limited.

risks.title: Technology and obsolescence risks
risks.score_rationale: The group is exposed to technology risks including equipment obsolescence, system compatibility issues, and potential product and service defects, which could impact revenues and net results.
